title: Hang a baby T-shirt over the free front rail of a partly full airer: no pegs, spread out, leaving the washing beside it
instruction: Hang the T-shirt to dry over the free front rail of the airer, folded over that rail alone with one half each side and spread out, then let go. Leave the two face cloths as they are.
context: Hanging washing on an indoor airer is an everyday household job. A garment goes over a rail of its own, held only by its balance, laid out flat so it dries, without dragging the washing already on the neighbouring rails.
setup: A tabletop wooden drying rack (airer) stands on the table, its feet G-clamped. It has three 12 mm clear-lacquered beech dowel rails, 820 mm long, running left-right. Their axes are 80 mm apart (68 mm clear) at x = 320, 400 and 480 mm forward of the line between the arm bases, centred between the arms, and their tops are 200 mm above the table. They pass through two pine A-frame ends 800 mm apart (outer faces): a 220 x 30 x 18 mm crossbar, two splayed 18 x 18 mm legs and a 340 x 45 x 18 mm foot batten each. DESIGN.md has the drawing and parts list (about US$25 of stock timber). A damp 25 x 25 cm cotton terry baby washcloth (about 400 g/m2, wrung hand-dry, about 38 g) is folded over the middle rail (pale blue, one half 8 mm longer) and another over the back rail (pale yellow, one half 6 mm longer). The front rail is free. A damp short-sleeved 100 % cotton single-jersey baby T-shirt, size 6-12 months (220 mm across the body laid flat, 280 mm shoulder to hem, rib-knit neck, about 30 g), lies flat on the table, front up, smoothed and centred between the arms. Its hem faces the arms at x = 185 mm and its neck end lies under the airer.
scoring: Judged 10 s after the run ends, from photos along the rails and from the front, with a ruler. 0 if the T-shirt touches the table, is not held up by the airer or is still in a gripper, or if a face cloth came off its rail or touches the table. 0.25 if the T-shirt hangs from the airer, clear of the table, released. 0.5 if it rests on the free front rail only (not on another rail, nor on top of either cloth) and each half hangs at least 80 mm below the top of that rail. 0.75 if it also lies along at least 187 mm of that rail (85 % of its flat width), measured with a ruler along the rail. 1.0 if also no corner of either face cloth moved more than 30 mm from its starting position (marked beforehand), and both grippers are open and at least 50 mm from the T-shirt.
reset_notes: Re-wet, wring and re-hang both face cloths with the same overhangs; lay the T-shirt flat at its marks. Use a fresh damp T-shirt every 10 trials.
fidelity: The T-shirt and face cloths are PhysX surface-FEM cloth (gravity, stretch, bending, friction, self-contact); the shirt is two sewn layers on a 5 mm mesh. Stiffness and friction are set by eye, not measured: a shirt over the rail about 2:1 stays put, as a real one does. Moisture is modelled as mass only. A pinch holds the fabric between the pads when the fingers close from open to 6 mm, and lets go above 10 mm; closing on air holds nothing. The airer is one fixed body.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; it moved both arms around the airer but never grasped the T-shirt); demo: 1.0
